evidence.quote: Weightbearing AP demonstrates complete loss of the medial femorotibial joint space with direct bone-on-bone apposition. Dense subchondral sclerosis of the medial tibial plateau and medial femoral condyle. Large marginal osteophytes medially and at the tibial spines.
IMPRESSION: End-stage medial compartment degenerative disease of the right knee with bone-on-bone apposition, subchondral sclerosis, and varus deformity.

results.explanation: The 07/23/2026 radiology report describes advanced (end-stage) degenerative disease with joint space narrowing (bone-on-bone), subchondral sclerosis, and large osteophytes, directly satisfying the criterion. An earlier report from 07/02/2026 described only mild change, but that is superseded/complemented by this later, more advanced imaging read by a different radiologist, and the surgeon's note acknowledges both films exist without resolving the discrepancy as an error, so the advanced findings stand as located evidence meeting the requirement.

evidence.quote: Night pain wakes him nightly. He has not had an unbroken night since the spring and looks it. He cannot kneel or squat, which is the substance of his trade, and he has been putting the tiling work out to a younger man and taking the money for supervising, which he describes as galling.

results.explanation: The surgical opinion note documents specific functional impacts of the knee pain: nightly night pain disrupting sleep, and inability to kneel or squat that has forced the patient to give up his trade of tiling, satisfying the requirement for documented functional impact.

evidence.quote: Meloxicam 15 mg daily. Started 03/11/2026 by Dr. Lindgren and taken every day as directed until he stopped it on 07/30/2026.
Attended 14 of 16 offered appointments over this episode.
No sustained benefit. He would report a good week and then lose it again, and by the last four visits there was no measurable change from where he started.
DISCHARGE Discharged. Further skilled therapy is not indicated.

results.explanation: The nursing intake note provides a dated start (03/11/2026) and dated stop (07/30/2026) of meloxicam, a conservative pharmacologic measure, spanning approximately 4.5 months, exceeding the 3-month threshold; the patient reported no benefit across this period. Independently, the physiotherapy discharge summary documents a completed physiotherapy episode that concluded with no sustained benefit and formal discharge, with the therapist explicitly stating that further skilled therapy is not indicated. Together these two independently-sourced records (medication record and physiotherapy record) corroborate that conservative management, of more than 3 months' duration, was attempted and failed.

results.explanation: The orthopedic surgeon's first-hand examination documents an antalgic gait, a measured range of motion deficit (15-90 degrees with a 15 degree fixed flexion contracture), and varus deformity of the right knee, all of which are functional limitations satisfying this criterion. - Nursing intake musculoskeletal assessment notes "No effusion. No deformity" but this is a general MSK exam, not specifically targeting infection markers (no mention of warmth, erythema, fever workup, wound status, or systemic infection signs).
- The preoperative assessment covers cardiovascular, respiratory, renal/hepatic/metabolic, haematology, and airway — but does not address infection status (no temperature noted at preop, no WBC, no mention of local or systemic infection screening).
- The nursing intake does record vitals including "T 36.6 C" which is a normal temperature, potentially bearing on systemic infection, but this is a routine vital sign rather than a targeted infection assessment, and no clinician draws a conclusion about infection from it.
- No passage anywhere states there is no active infection, nor performs a targeted examination or investigation for infection (local or systemic).

This is a case where the topic is not named or targeted anywhere in the record — vitals are routine observations, not an infection-focused evaluation capable of excluding infection.
